items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: his idol at the time was Frankie Trumbauer. A lot of people may not realize it, but he was around when Lester played alto.

ctx.x: at all -- but he wouldn't be judged on his personality; he would be judged on what he was doing with his feet, so, you know, I think that phase of it was very, very interesting -- but I used to dance and sing all the time, you know, on the TOBA circuit, and after we left the TOBA circuit, we moved to Minnesota -- to Minneapolis, and I was going to grammar school. But that's when my dad formed a band in Minneapolis. And, as a matter of fact, the Pettifords were also from Minneapolis because Lester used to hang out…

But I don't think you ever heard a musician practice more or diligently than Lester did. At that time when we were in Minneapolis, you know, he was a young guy, because I was in grammar school, and his idol at the time was Frankie Trumbauer. A lot of people may not realize it, but he was around when Lester played alto.

And he used to play all of these Frankie Trumbauer records in his room, and I used to hear -- Frankie Trumbauer used to make a lot of records that was -- well, he was running over the horn, and all along, you know?
